add.title: Grenada Stakeholder Report for the UN Universal Periodic Review: LGBTIQ+ Rights (The Advocates for Human Rights, Khaleem Ali, GrenCHAP)
add.summary: UN UPR stakeholder report (submitted 11 Oct 2024): because Grenada has no laws permitting legal gender change, 'the Government also prosecutes transgender women – who are considered legal men under the law.' The report provides no prison-specific housing/segregation detail, but it establishes the operative placement framework: a trans person's legal status, and so any correctional classification, follows registered/birth sex rather than gender identity. No special unit, solitary/segregation practice, or trans-prisoner housing case/ruling is documented for Grenada.

add.title: Grenada 2023 Human Rights Report (US State Dept)
add.summary: US State Dept 2023 report (pub. Feb 2024): Grenada's sole penitentiary, designed for about 200 persons, held 385 prisoners as of August 2023, including six women in a separate block; conditions were harsh due to gross overcrowding, with potable water in men's-block hallways but not cells. The report documents gendered blocks and general detention conditions but records no transgender-specific housing policy, special unit, or segregation practice, and no trans-prisoner cases or complaints.
